name: Finance Leadership and Operating Model
description: How the CFO learns the business, sets priorities, structures the finance team, and runs the operating rhythm with the CEO, the board, and functional leaders.
outcome: A clear finance charter, a sequenced 12-month plan, a staffed team with defined ownership, and a predictable meeting and reporting calendar the whole company can rely on.

name: Accounting and Controllership
description: The books: monthly close, chart of accounts, reconciliations, consolidation, revenue recognition, technical accounting positions, fixed assets, and audit readiness.
outcome: Financial statements that close on a published calendar, reconcile to supporting detail, follow written policy, and survive an external audit without surprises.

name: Strategic Finance and Planning
description: The forward view: three-statement model, annual operating plan, rolling forecast, scenarios, KPI definitions, budget versus actual analysis, board analytics, and deal evaluation.
outcome: One trusted model and one KPI dictionary that drive planning, resourcing decisions, board reporting, and capital allocation across the company.

name: Commercial and Revenue Finance
description: Finance embedded in go-to-market: pricing and packaging, bookings and pipeline analytics, deal desk, commissions, quote-to-cash, collections strategy, capacity planning, and unit economics.
outcome: Deals that are priced and approved with known margin, a clean path from quote to cash, and unit economics the leadership team and board actually believe.

name: Finance Operations, Systems, and Data
description: The plumbing: ERP and subledgers, integrations to billing, payroll, expense, procurement and equity systems, master data, access, automation, and finance reporting infrastructure.
outcome: A documented system architecture where data flows automatically between systems, reconciles by design, and produces reporting without spreadsheet rework.

name: Treasury, Capital, and Investor Relations
description: Cash and capital: daily cash visibility, the 13-week forecast, banking redundancy, investment policy, debt and covenants, currency exposure, fundraising, and investor reporting.
outcome: Cash is visible daily, protected across more than one institution, invested under written policy, and runway decisions are made with a forecast the board trusts.

name: Tax
description: Federal, state, and local income tax, sales and use tax nexus, research credits, payroll tax coordination, international tax, transfer pricing, and provision readiness.
outcome: Every filing obligation is known, calendared, and met on time, with credits captured and exposure quantified before it becomes a diligence finding.

name: Risk, Controls, and Internal Audit
description: Risk register, segregation of duties, delegated authority, fraud and payment controls, access reviews, third-party risk, lightweight SOX readiness, control testing, and whistleblower process.
outcome: The company knows its top risks, who owns them, which controls mitigate them, and can show evidence that those controls are tested and working.

name: People, Payroll, and Equity
description: Workforce planning, compensation structure, payroll governance and accuracy, cap table integrity, equity grants, option pool sizing, 409A valuations, dilution, and international employment cost.
outcome: Headcount plans tie to the model, payroll runs under control, and the cap table reconciles to board approvals so equity decisions are made with real dilution math.

name: Governance, Legal, Entity, and Insurance
description: Board approvals and calendar, corporate records and entity standing, franchise tax filings, the contracts interface with legal, directors and officers coverage, cyber and other insurance, and international entity readiness.
outcome: Corporate records are complete and current, board approvals are documented before action, and insurance coverage matches the company's actual risk profile.
